weapons.name: Competition 1911 5" stainless, adjustable target sights
weapons.source_note: GUNSweek review of the Colt Competition Pistol, specification line: "Barrel National Match barrel: 127 mm / 5\"; six LH grooves, 1:16\" twist". Body text: "a 5\"-long, National Match cold-hammer forged out of stainless steel, with a bright shiny polish and six left-handed grooves and a 1-in-16\" pitch". States the Colt Competition Pistol barrel has six left-hand grooves and one turn in 16 inches = 406.4 mm per turn.

weapons.name: Defender 3" barrel, compact carry 1911
weapons.source_note: Fusion Firearms "1911 Defender Barrel Selector - Ultra Match Grade" (3" Defender-size 1911 barrel), DETAILS: "3\" defender size, perfect for a compact and versatile pistol ... 45acp, 40S&W/10mm: 1:16 twist rate", and "Twist rate 45acp, 40S&W/10mm = 1:16". The barrel maker states one turn in 16 inches = 406.4 mm per turn for the Defender-size .45 ACP barrel. No Colt factory document stating the Defender twist was found.

weapons.name: MP7 Submachine Gun
weapons.source_note: C.I.P. TDCC Tab I datasheet for the 4,6 x 30 (4.6×30 mm) cartridge, "Barrel / Grooves" block: "N = 6" and "u = 150.00". In the C.I.P. TDCC drawing u is the twist (pitch of rifling) in millimetres, so the standard twist is one turn in 150.00 mm with 6 grooves. Heckler & Koch's own MP7A1 Technical Data sheet (hk-manuals) states "Barrel profile/Twist: Polygonal profile, 6 twist lines, right-hand twist" but gives no pitch.
